newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: RUBBER - Southeast Asian prices seen drifting lower.
newsitem.headline: RUBBER - Southeast Asian prices seen drifting lower.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber markets are expected to drift lower this week with activity slowed by the upcoming festival period in the region, but prices may now be approaching their nadir, traders said on Monday.
Malaysian traders said limited consumer demand could keep their market in the doldrums with prices softening further.

"There have not been many inquiries since the beginning of the year and we don't expect buyers to return so soon," said one dealer. She said most consumers were well covered with some having bought up to April/May positions.
Traders said though Malaysian prices have been on a downtrend, they need to come off further in order to beat off competition from lower-priced rubber in Thailand and Indonesia.

An ample supply of raw materials following an improvement in weather conditions had also weighed on prices. But, dealers said further downside should be limited as producers were unlikely to sell at much lower levels.
"There were already not many sellers at current levels. I don't think prices can come down very much from here," said another local dealer.

Traders said the twin festivals of Chinese Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr next month, when plantations stop tapping rubber for nearly a week, should not affect supply as stocks were at a comfortable level due to the lack of offtake.

At the close of last week, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the benchmark February RSS 1 buyer at 302 cents a kg, down from 304 cents the previous week. February SMR 20 buyer was at 297 cents against 299.50.
Drum latex was offered by trading houses at 235 cents a kg FOB on Friday.

In Indonesia, the price of benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices is seen remaining weak in coming days amid slow foreign demand and thin supply due to the Ramadhan fasting month, local dealers said.

They said March SIR20 offer prices were seen remaining weak and ranging between 54.00-54.25 U.S. cents a lb FOB Medan, 53.75-54.00 FOB Surabaya, Padang and Palembang and at 53.25-53.50 FOB Pontianak and Jambi.
"Sentiment is likely to stay weak while prices are expected to remain under pressure due to the slow demand," one Jakarta dealer said.
In the latex market dealers said they expected to see few significant deals done in the short-term.
January high amoniac grade latex was seen remaining on offer at 2,150 rupiah/kg in Bandung and Tangerang and at 2,200 rupiah in Medan.
In Thailand, rubber prices have been steady to lower, moving in a narrow range with a downward bias throughout the week in dull trade, local trade sources said.
"Although the supplies started to drop, lack of buying interest pressured the prices," said one Hat Yai dealer.
The volume of rubber entering the market last week was 44,236 kg, almost a 10 percent drop from the previous week.

Supplies from the south of the country remain high, but those from the northeast and the east have dwindled due to the onset of the wintering season in these areas which will be followed by the south.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for February shipment was quoted around US$1.20-1.22 a kg FOB Bangkok on Friday,compared with $1.22-1.23 in the previous week.
Latex was quoted around $0.91-0.93 a kg on the same basis.
"But I heard some southern traders offered as low as $0.90 which I cannot compete with because the supplies around my area are getting tight," said a trader in the eastern region.
Some traders were optimistic that buying interest would emerge soon.
"We hope to see support soon. The current price levels should be attractive enough to lure buyers into the market again. After Chinese new year, the activity should pick up," said one Bangkok trader.
-- With contributions from Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta, Bangkok
